title: Revelation 6:9–17
context: The fifth seal reveals the souls of martyrs under the altar crying out for justice. They receive white robes and are told to wait until the number of their fellow servants is complete. The sixth seal brings cosmic upheaval, and people of every rank hide from the face of the one on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb.

verses.text: When he opened the fifth seal, I saw underneath the altar the souls of those who had been killed for the Word of God, and for the testimony of the Lamb which they had.
verses.arminianNotes: The martyrs were killed for the word of God and their testimony. Arminian readers see faithful witnesses who held fast to the end.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the souls under the altar as the faithful dead, alive with God before the resurrection.

verses.text: They cried with a loud voice, saying, “How long, Master, the holy and true, until you judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?”
verses.arminianNotes: “How long?” echoes the psalms of lament. The cry is for justice, not personal revenge. Arminian readers see God hearing the prayers of the suffering.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the prayer as an appeal to God’s holy justice, which he will answer in his time.

verses.text: A long white robe was given to each of them. They were told that they should rest yet for a while, until their fellow servants and their brothers, who would also be killed even as they were, should complete their course.
verses.arminianNotes: The martyrs are given white robes and told to rest until the number of their fellow servants is complete. Arminian readers see God’s patience allowing more time for the gospel and for repentance.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers often see in the “number” God’s fixed purpose, with history moving toward an appointed completion.
verses.keyContrast: Arminian readers see the delay as God’s patience and the time it allows for repentance. Reformed readers see a number known to God and a history moving toward its appointed end.

verses.text: I saw when he opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake. The sun became black as sackcloth made of hair, and the whole moon became as blood.
verses.arminianNotes: The sixth seal brings an earthquake and darkened sun and moon. Some read this as literal cosmic collapse at the end, while others read it as prophetic imagery for the fall of powers, as in Isaiah 13 and Joel 2.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same range of interpretations, with many seeing the language of the final day.

verses.text: The stars of the sky fell to the earth, like a fig tree dropping its unripe figs when it is shaken by a great wind.
verses.arminianNotes: Falling stars like unripe figs shaken by wind continue the imagery of upheaval.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the shaking of the created order before the Judge.

verses.text: The sky was removed like a scroll when it is rolled up. Every mountain and island was moved out of its place.
verses.arminianNotes: The sky rolled up like a scroll echoes Isaiah 34:4.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the end of the present order.

verses.text: The kings of the earth, the princes, the commanding officers, the rich, the strong, and every slave and free person, hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains.
verses.arminianNotes: People of every rank, from kings to slaves, hide. No status protects anyone in the day of judgment.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see all people equal before God’s judgment.

verses.text: They told the mountains and the rocks, “Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him who sits on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb,
verses.arminianNotes: “The wrath of the Lamb” is a striking phrase. The one who was slain is also the judge. Arminian readers see that rejecting the Lamb’s grace leaves only his judgment.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Christ as both Savior and Judge, and the terror of those who face him without refuge in his grace.

verses.text: for the great day of his wrath has come, and who is able to stand?”
verses.arminianNotes: “Who is able to stand?” Chapter 7 answers the question with the sealed servants and the great multitude.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the answer in chapter 7: those sealed by God and washed in the Lamb’s blood.
